capabilities.local_comparison: Compare two local controller solves at the same saved state/previous input/horizon with exactly one adopted weight change. capabilities.prediction_braking: At one saved projected state, compare recorded input with instantaneous braking-box input over the fixed short horizon. Can measure local endpoint speed/position differences. Cannot separate objective weighting, seed selection, horizon effects or backend-model mismatch when they predict the same result; cannot identify the dominant settling cause.

attribution.reason: 34 of 35 updates ended as User_Requested_Stop with one Solve_Succeeded, sampled solves took about 15 s against a 0.01 s control period, and sampled selections are iteration 0 with policy stop reason budget_best_feasible while one accepted plan was applied, so the applied plans may be seed/shallow iterates rather than converged plans. This is consistent with the observed signals but does not establish settling causality: the scheduling note states wall deadline misses do not inject physical delay into simulated time, and no closed-loop counterfactual replay exists. Selected-iteration records are also incomplete for a full run-wide picture in the views read.

Recorded weights place terminal_weight 5.0 against velocity_weight 0.0001, terminal_velocity_weight 0.0001 and terminal_tip_speed_weight 0.0, and terminal reach was met while tip speed remained 0.63517 m/s, which is consistent with a position-dominated terminal objective. Raw weight magnitudes do not establish cost-term importance without actual contributions and scaling, and a single execution cannot separate weighting from seed selection, horizon effects or projected-model mismatch.

Projection residuals of 0.66-2.92 rad/m and predicted-versus-measured tip velocity differences of about 0.022-0.024 m/s in the sampled late window show the projected model and the serial backend endpoint disagree locally, which could degrade plan quality. The available views cannot separate model mismatch from objective weighting, seed selection or horizon effects that would predict the same endpoint difference, and no full backend replay is available.

Inventory source.force_limits lists 8.0 N per channel, and the sampled late applied vector (update 29) peaks at 7.02 N, below that limit, but per-update force_limit_saturated and tension_tracking_error_n signals were not read for the late window, so saturation-driven loss of braking authority is neither supported nor excluded.

The execution metadata states that synchronous controller calls complete before fixed-count backend steps and that wall deadline misses do not inject physical delay into simulated time, so the 35 deadline misses cannot by themselves produce the physical tip speed and position error observed in the settling window.

request_content.question: Why does secondary (settling) performance remain unmet in this execution even though terminal reach succeeded? The question is open: which of the retained signals — per-update solve/status behaviour, plan/iteration selection, effective horizon, applied versus requested tension, projected-state evolution, sampled backend motion at matched endpoints — are consistent with a sustained late-window tip speed and position error after reach, and which remain indeterminate with available evidence? No root cause is presumed; a single bounded projected-model probe over a 10 ms horizon cannot by itself explain an entire settling failure and must not be presented as doing so.
